subject: Private VPC control-plane switchover drill — ZenithBank scope
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@zenithbank.eu>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:03:00 +0100
Subject: Private VPC control-plane switchover drill — request and constraints

Hi David,

Thanks again for the earlier conversation. We need to validate how Redwood’s private deployment behaves when we execute a control-plane driven switchover between our EU primary VPC and an APAC warm-standby. Before we schedule any live work, can you confirm the following at a high level so our legal/compliance team can sign off on a drill: 

- Will any EU-resident PII or tenant metadata be replicated to APAC control-plane services during a switchover/drill? We need assurance that persistent data remains within EU-bound storage.
- How do you handle KV cache and prefix caching during a staged switchover? Is any cache persisted to disk or to a regionally-located object store?
- KMS behavior: are customer keys (CMKs) ever staged/temporarily exported to non-EU regions?
- Network egress: what egress IPs should our firewall team expect during a drill, and can you run through the minimal network ACL changes required?

We can provide a short list of allowed test client IPs. Attached is our preflight questionnaire (Zenith_preflight_questions.xlsx) — it mostly mirrors our compliance checklist. Ideally we’d like to run a controlled drill during the week of 14 Sep.

Can you share a one-page outline we can give to our compliance group and a tentative runbook?

Best,
Maria Lopez
Head of Cloud Operations
ZenithBank Ltd.

Attachment: Zenith_preflight_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@zenithbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 18:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private VPC control-plane switchover drill — request and constraints

Maria — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then next steps and attachments:

- Persistent tenant data: Redwood Private keeps customer persistent stores (S3/GCS-equivalent volumes, DB replicas) in the region(s) you designate. For ZenithBank’s configuration, your production blobs and DB replicas stay in EU. During a control-plane initiated switchover we do not copy persistent tenant data to APAC.

- KV/cache handling: runtime-only KV and prefix caches are in-memory on serving nodes. For warm-standby scenarios we stream a minimal KV checkpoint to an encrypted object store; for Zenith’s default profile we can configure that store to remain in EU only (no cross-region replication).

- KMS: we never export CMKs. We can either integrate with your EU KMS (recommended) or use a Redwood-managed customer master key that is region-scoped to the EU. We will not stage keys in APAC.

- Network egress: I’ve attached a brief outline that lists the IP ranges and ports used for control-plane and data-plane orchestration. Short answer: you will need to open outbound to our control-plane orchestration endpoints and to the warm-standby egress pool for ephemeral health checks.

I’ve attached a one-page outline (redwood-private-drill-outline.pdf) and a proposed quick runbook for a non-production dry-run. Proposed next steps:
1) Internal technical call (we suggest 45 minutes) with your Ops + network teams to walk the outline.
2) Send the whitelist of test client IPs & any contract references.
3) We’ll prepare a short mutual action plan and a preflight checklist.

If the week of 14 Sep is still the target, I can block time on 14/15 for the call.

Cheers,
David Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-drill-outline.pdf (2 pages), controlplane-egress-ipranges.csv (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC control-plane switchover drill — network & runtime notes (internal)

David / Marissa — internal tech notes for the drill. Copying relevant bits into the runbook before we send: 

- Control-plane state: our control plane uses ephemeral orchestration tokens and does not persist tenant PII. Metadata required for routing (tenant-id mappings, model version pins) are stored in an EU-scoped metadata DB for Zenith. That DB is read-only from APAC control-plane nodes unless we explicitly permit a write during a forced failover window — we should avoid that.

- Cache checkpointing: we write checkpoints as encrypted objects with SSE using your CMK ARN. For Zenith, configure the checkpoint bucket with region-scoped replication=off.

- KMS: confirm via integration that we will use your CMK in EU (no fallback to Redwood-managed keys unless explicitly authorized). If the customer requires, we can add an HSM-backed policy to deny key usage outside the EU region.

- Network: minimal ports 443 (control), 10250 (k8s health probes between nodes), 5000-5100 (ephemeral agent tunnels). For the drill we will run a short burst of outbound health checks from the APAC warm-standby — ensure your firewall allows the egress pool 18.210.0.0/18 and 35.204.128.0/18 (we will provide exact ranges in the preflight).

- Blast radius controls: canaries only, limited to 5% of traffic on the edge route, and rollback is automatic within 30s on failed health checks. For a compliance run we recommend 0% production traffic — use a staging tenant id.

Attachments: network-sip-notes.txt (text, 5KB)

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
